title: Shrinkflation and Consumer Demand
eligible_reason: Not a binary staggered DiD. The demand estimations (Code/9_Demand_Estimations.R, 10_Demand_Estimations_Interaction.R) regress log(units + 0.5) on log(imputed_price) and log(size1_amount) with store-product and week FE (or store-product-week-of-year and store-product-year FE, or quarterly time FE), plus IV versions and ShrinkingProduct x log price / log size interactions. Package size changes occur at product-specific dates, but they enter as a continuous log-size regressor alongside continuous price, so the estimands are price and size elasticities, not a binary post-adoption effect. Remaining scripts produce descriptive tables and figures (prevalence of shrinkflation, average price/size changes).
design_notes: R fixest::feols, NielsenIQ RMS store-week scanner data 2006-2019 (Kilts), estimation by product group; base-price imputation algorithm (C++). Abstract: consumers scarcely adjust demand despite higher per-ounce prices.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: continuous regressors log price and log size; IV variants

data_files_note: README: NielsenIQ RMS/HMS data via Kilts Center; not shipped. Package ships code, RA coding spreadsheets and the imputation algorithm only.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text). Continuous size/price demand design; licensed data not shipped.
